newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TNT'S GD Express posts first profit.
newsitem.headline: TNT'S GD Express posts first profit.

text.p: Transport group TNT Ltd said on Wednesday that its GD Express Worldwide Group posted its first ever pre-tax profit in the year to June 30, 1996, but that this was lower than expected.
"GD Express increased revenues by 9.6 percent in local currency terms and earned a small profit before tax for the first time," TNT said in releasing its group results.
"The result was lower than expected due to slowing global economic conditions, particularly in Europe where the majority of GDEW's revenue is sourced," TNT said.
GE Express is 50 percent owned by TNT and 50 percent owned by the Dutch and Swedish post offices.
After tax and abnormals, however, TNT's accounts show its losses falling to A$6.22 million from A$11.57 million in 1994/95.
"The operation has made very substantial progress over the last four years from making significant losses to profitability," TNT said.
"The continued improvement of GDEW's performance reflects tight cost controls and focus on improving revenue quality," it said.
During the year GD Express World announced the relocation of its European hub operation from Cologne in Germany to Liege in Belgium.
"The Liege hub is due to begin operations in 1998 and will provide for future expansion of GD Express' operations."
TNT's shares were unchanged at A$1.44 at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
